messages:
jamie (support): Customer on prod-us-east-1 seeing large spike in latency and 502/401s after traffic shifted yesterday. billing alert + customer upset.

linda (cs): Customer report: requests routed to eu-west and auth fails, tokens rejected. They say headers show X-Region: us-east but responses from eu-west.

nina (oncall): looks like region hint being ignored somewhere in L7 path. Can you paste one failing request/response?

jamie (support): Pasted sanitized curl: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "X-Region: us-east" https://api.redwood.ai/generate
```
Response: 502 Bad Gateway, Via: envoy, X-Served-Region: eu-west-1, set-cookie: session=deleted; Path=/; HttpOnly

kai (edge-sre): Interesting — envoy adding X-Served-Region from egress VIP. Could be an upstream header rewrite on the VIP swap. We had a config push 02:15UTC that swapped a VIP between pools.

jamie (support): Customer repro steps: 1) set X-Region: us-east in header 2) send high concurrency POSTs 3) ~30% go to eu-west and fail auth (401) or 502 if backend closed connection.

nina (oncall): Quick check: are we stripping or overwriting X-Region anywhere? `envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata` or a Lua filter?

kai (edge-sre): Found a Lua header-normalize filter in gateway-v2 that runs only on the VIP that got swapped. It rewrites `X-Region` to `region` lowercase and then `header_to_metadata` expects `X-Region`. For swapped VIP the rewrite occurred after routing decision so routing used fallback (region-less) -> cross-region.

jamie (support): So ordering bug: rewrite then route? or route then rewrite?

kai (edge-sre): Exactly. On normal path the rewrite never ran. After the VIP swap the filter executed on an upstream edge path causing rewrite earlier. Result: routing policy saw no `X-Region` header -> smart-routing sent to cheapest available region (eu-west) -> auth tokens bound to us-east rejected -> 401; session mismatch cause backend closes -> 502 cascade.

nina (oncall): Short-term mitigation: re-add a fallback header-preserve rule in the gateway filter chain to copy `x-region` into metadata before any rewrite. I pushed patch `gw-hotfix-1755` to canary (2 instances) at 13:12UTC.

jamie (support): Customer confirms reduced cross-region hits after canary. Still seeing occasional 502s during spikes.

kai (edge-sre): Need a permanent fix: reorder filters so header->metadata happens first and remove the unexpected rewrite on the VIP swap path. Also add unit test for VIP swap path. I'll open PR and tag nina for rollout policy.

nina (oncall): Plan: 1) merge filter-order PR with integration test 2) full rollout to gateways in batches 3) monitor routing by `X-Served-Region` metric and auth 4) rollback plan is previous gateway config. Target: roll by EOD.

linda (cs): I'll update the customer with the mitigation and ETA. Thanks for fast triage :thumbsup:

sre-bot: deploy-bot: CANARY DEPLOY gw-hotfix-1755 -> 2/12 gateways successful (13:12UTC).

jamie (support): Root cause summary for ticket: VIP swap exposed a filter ordering bug in the gateway where a header normalization rewrote region hints before they were persisted to routing metadata, causing cross-region failover and auth failures.

nina (oncall): Follow-ups: add alert for `x_served_region_mismatch_rate` and add canary traffic test that asserts `X-Region` hints are honored during VIP changes.

kai (edge-sre): PR: https://git.internal/redwood/gateway/pull/4325 — includes fix + integration test. Will schedule rollover 15m after merge.

jamie (support): Customer updated: accepted ETA and moving to monitoring. Closing the escalation once rollout completes and metrics look stable.

linda (cs): marking as prioritized for postmortem and billing credit review.
